outcome: WON on attempt 1, 7 turns, 2 player faints - a real fight. Levels kept.
supersedes: The previous receipt recorded outcome 'NOT PLAYABLE - blocked by a content defect' (E0014-PARTYSIZE-0). That defect is repaired: TRAINER_GINA_AND_MIA_1 now compiles with a four-member party and the battle started and ran to completion. This receipt is the first real play of E0014.
party_manifest_note: The manifest was rebuilt for this run. The earlier one (Weavile/Whimsicott/Lucario/Arcanine/Porygon-Z/Snorlax) was chronology-illegal for a Route 104 battle: Sneasel is wild:Seaspray_Cave_B1F, Cottonee is wild:VerdanturfMeadow, Lucario and Porygon-Z are wild:AlteringCave_1F and Munchlax is wild:Route116, all of which are maps a player reaches AFTER Route 104 (Verdanturf Meadow only after RusturfTunnel at play_order 29, cap 20). The replacement party uses only Route101/102/103/104/PetalburgWoods roots.
opponent_levels_medium: PLUSLE 14, MINUN 14, VOLBEAT 16, ILLUMISE 16 (cap 14; offsets 2/2/4/4, Medium -2)

attempts.player_faint_detail: Arcanine (53/53, full HP, Intimidate already applied) was KOed on turn 1 by focused Plus/Minus-boosted Thunderbolts from both rodents. Jolteon was KOed on turn 6 by Illumise's Bug Buzz after Volbeat's +2 Bug Buzz had already taken it to 3/46.
attempts.note: A genuine fight. A 2-HP Volbeat survived four extra turns on Prankster Roost and one Protect, and the twins traded two of my six for four of their four.

strategy_checks.check: Plusle/Minun Plus+Minus shared special-attack boost while both are active
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1: both L14 rodents chose MOVE_THUNDERBOLT into battler 0 and the pair killed a full-HP 53 HP L14 Arcanine outright (Fire takes Electric neutrally, and Intimidate does nothing to a special attack). Two unboosted L14 Thunderbolts do not reach 53; the shared Plus/Minus 1.5x is the only way that board resolves.

strategy_checks.check: Helping Hand chosen only when it beats two attacks
strategy_checks.evidence: Helping Hand never appeared across the whole battle. On turn 1 two attacks scored a clean KO, which is exactly the condition the dossier sets; afterwards the pair was never both alive and both able to attack the same target.

strategy_checks.check: Minun Light Screen / Encore only against a relevant threat
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2: Minun chose MOVE_LIGHT_SCREEN with my two remaining bodies being special attackers (Jolteon Thunderbolt/Shadow Ball, Sylveon Hyper Voice/Mystical Fire). The screen measurably worked - Sylveon's Mystical Fire fell from 19 to ~13 per hit and Volbeat survived several turns behind it. Soft note: the final turn 8 Light Screen was near-worthless (Minun alone at 12/45, no partner to protect, killed by Rock Slide the same turn). Encore never fired; nothing on my side was ever locked into a move worth Encoring.

strategy_checks.check: Volbeat priority Tail Glow converted into Bug Buzz damage
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2: Volbeat entered and immediately used Prankster MOVE_TAIL_GLOW ('Sp. Atk rose drastically', +3) before anything else on the board moved. Turn 3: MOVE_BUG_BUZZ into Jolteon did 43 of 46 HP. That is the authored engine firing on the first two turns it was on the field, and it cost me a Pokemon.

strategy_checks.check: Illumise priority Encore / Helping Hand in the firefly mode
strategy_checks.evidence: Illumise only entered on turn 5 (switched in for a 12/45 Minun) with the board already decided. It chose MOVE_BUG_BUZZ (KO on the 3 HP Jolteon, turn 6) and MOVE_DAZZLING_GLEAM (spread, super effective on Heracross, turn 7). Both are the correct direct-damage choices on those boards; Prankster Encore had no target locked into anything and Helping Hand had no partner able to convert it. Declining them was right, so this is 'no opportunity', not a failure.

strategy_checks.check: Roost/Protect must buy useful future damage rather than sustain an empty setup loop
strategy_checks.result: PASS - the best guard play in this block
strategy_checks.evidence: See the Protect ledger. Volbeat at 2/61 survived turns 4, 5, 6 and 7 on priority Roost plus one Protect, and it took Rock Slide plus Hyper Voice together to finish it.

strategy_checks.check: Ground attacks / Electric immunity / priority denial / Taunt as counterplay (the authored crack)
strategy_checks.result: PASS - the crack works as documented
strategy_checks.evidence: Volt Absorb Jolteon changed the AI's targeting immediately: from turn 3 on Minun aimed every Thunderbolt at Sylveon (battler 2) and never once fed the immunity. Fairy and Rock spread damage from Sylveon and Heracross is what actually ended the fight - Rock Slide was 2x on both fireflies and killed Illumise and Minun.

protect_ledger.payoff: NOT EMPTY - saved its life twice over. It blocked Jolteon's Thunderbolt (which had been doing ~32 a hit, lethal from 2 HP) and Sylveon's Hyper Voice. Volbeat then got two more turns of Roost out of the reprieve and forced me to spend a double spread attack to remove it.

NOT EMPTY. Turn 4 Roost from 6 HP outpaced Thunderbolt; turn 5 Roost from 4 HP did the same; turn 7 Roost from 2 HP forced the KO to come from two attacks in the same turn. Three heals off a 61 HP body kept the trainer's setup piece alive from turn 4 to turn 7.

NOT EMPTY. A genuine escape: Minun was in Hyper Voice range and was preserved to come back as the last body. The new turn-one healthy-switch charge did not suppress a switch that was actually needed, which is the intended shape.

ai_observations.board: Minun alone at 12/45, no partner, facing Heracross (26/50) and Sylveon (36/63). Rock Slide was lethal to it whatever it did.
ai_observations.assessment: Not scored as a defect. Both actions lose, and the new next-turn pricing is supposed to pay a screen only when its owner survives the turn - here it did not, so the value banked should have been zero. Worth one look at whether a side-status effect is being priced for a battler that is about to be the last faint; the damage line was strictly better by a small margin.

level_rationale: Brief rule 5: 'Won with 2+ faints or after a real fight -> keep.' Two of my six died, one of them a full-HP lead on turn 1, and the trainer's authored engine (Tail Glow -> Bug Buzz) executed and earned one of those kills. PLUSLE 2 / MINUN 2 / VOLBEAT 4 / ILLUMISE 4 are correct as authored.
cooler_note: Yes, and it is close already. The two paired modes genuinely played differently: the rodents are a burst-damage lead that killed something on turn one, and the fireflies are a priority setup-and-sustain core that refused to die. The weak half is Illumise, which is a softer copy of Volbeat rather than a second idea - it arrived, used two attacking moves and added nothing the trainer did not already have. Suggestion for a later pass, not applied here (unchanged from the previous receipt and now confirmed in play): give Illumise Baton Pass or Struggle Bug so the firefly mode can move Volbeat's Tail Glow boost, which would turn the Roost stall into a genuine relay instead of a delay.
authored_set_legality: Clean. All four members, abilities, items and moves resolve correctly at cap 14 and every move in every set is present and usable in the compiled party. No legality problem found.

content_defects_resolved.evidence: src/data/trainers.party TRAINER_GINA_AND_MIA_1 now carries a four-member body that the ROM instantiates: Plusle L14, Minun L14, Volbeat L16, Illumise L16 all appeared on the field in run work/playtest/13-GINA_AND_MIA_1/r1.

not_finished: Illumise's Prankster Encore and Helping Hand are still unobserved - it only ever entered on a decided board. A future run that removes the rodents first and leaves the fireflies a live partner would exercise the second mode properly.
